stem: Two independent machines run a night shift. The odds against the first breaking down are 3 to 2, and the odds against the second breaking down are 7 to 3. What is the probability, to two decimals, that exactly one of the two machines breaks down during the shift?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Odds against a to b give P(event) = b/(a+b). So P(first breaks) = 2/5 = 0.4 and P(second breaks) = 3/10 = 0.3. Exactly one = P(first only) + P(second only) = 0.4*0.7 + 0.3*0.6 = 0.28 + 0.18 = 0.46.
Computes P(at least one breaks) = 1 - (0.6)(0.7) = 0.58, which counts the both-break case too. 'Exactly one' excludes the case where both fail.
Reports P(both break) = 0.4*0.3 = 0.12, the intersection, instead of the symmetric-difference probability for exactly one.
Adds the two breakdown probabilities 0.4 + 0.3 = 0.7, ignoring that this double counts the both-break overlap and overcounts. Independent events that can co-occur are not mutually exclusive.

explanation: Odds against a to b mean P(event) = b/(a+b), so P(first breaks) = 2/(3+2) = 0.4 and P(second breaks) = 3/(7+3) = 0.3. 'Exactly one' is the symmetric difference: P(first and not second) + P(second and not first) = 0.4*(1-0.3) + 0.3*(1-0.4) = 0.28 + 0.18 = 0.46. This deliberately excludes both the neither-breaks and both-break cases.

explanation_sections.punchline: Odds against a to b give P = b/(a+b), the smaller share. 'Exactly one' = P(A)(1-P(B)) + P(B)(1-P(A)); it drops both the both-fail and neither-fail cases.
explanation_sections.approach: Model: independent events, exactly-one. First read odds against correctly: the favourable count is the second number, so P = b/(a+b), giving 0.4 and 0.3. Then build exactly-one as two disjoint products, each event times the other's complement, and add. Do not use 1 - P(none); that is at-least-one and keeps the both-fail term.
explanation_sections.lesson: P(exactly one of A, B) = P(A) + P(B) - 2 P(A) P(B) for independent events. It is strictly less than P(at least one), which keeps the intersection.
explanation_sections.timing: About 165 seconds: two odds conversions, two products, one sum. Reject 0.58 fast, it is P(at least one) and wrongly includes the both-break case.
